title: Authentication and identity providers
status: AUTHORED. Technique layer partially in web-attack-atlas W07 (queued, pointer declared).

atom_notes.A03: the core primitive: the system misidentifies who is acting
atom_notes.A09: token and signature properties that are assumed and are not
atom_notes.A14: the human in the flow: MFA fatigue, device code consent, helpdesk reset
atom_notes.A04: session and token state that diverges from the real authorisation state
atom_notes.A05: assertion and claim shape confusion, audience and scope handling

required_cells.why: capture the whole auth flow including redirects before testing any of it
know whether the protocol is local, federated or both before choosing attacks
enumeration, lockout and policy probing need automation and care
token and assertion tampering is the exploitation step
a token accepted is not a finding until you show what it grants
auth findings need account takeover framing or they get downgraded
retest after credential policy or validation changes
drift detection on IdP and client configuration

entries.name: jwt_tool
entries.role: The full JWT attack set: none, algorithm confusion, kid traversal, jku injection, claim tampering
preconditions: the verifier accepts a header you can influence
detected_by: alg or kid mismatch at the verifier
entries.note: Runs all tests with -M at, then a specific tamper with -T. Start there, not with a hand written payload.

entries.name: hydra
entries.role: Online credential testing against a login form or basic auth, with lockout awareness
preconditions: no lockout, or a lockout policy you have tested
detected_by: failed login distribution per IP and per account
entries.note: The lockout test matters more than the cracking. Run one account first and watch for lockout before any list.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: medusa
entries.role: Parallel credential testing, useful when per-IP rate limits are absent
detected_by: failed login distribution per IP and per account
entries.note: Parallelism is both the feature and the reason to be careful: it is the fastest way to lock out every account at once.

entries.name: mitmproxy
entries.role: Capture the whole auth flow, including redirects, tokens and cookie transitions
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: ffuf
entries.role: Username and account enumeration via response and timing differentials
preconditions: an auth endpoint that behaves differently for known and unknown accounts
oracle: status, length or timing cluster separating existent from non existent
detected_by: response or timing difference for unknown accounts

entries.name: nuclei
entries.role: Known auth misconfiguration and default credential templates before manual work
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: JWT Editor (Burp extension)
entries.role: Interactive JWT manipulation inside the proxy, pairs with jwt_tool for the exploit path
oracle: modified token accepted by the server
claim change reflected in the session
detected_by: alg or kid mismatch at the verifier
entries.note: BApp store deep links change. Link goes to the store; search for JWT Editor.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: SAML Raider (Burp extension)
entries.role: SAML assertion manipulation, signature stripping and XSW attacks
preconditions: SAML SSO in front of the app
detected_by: signature not verified over the signed element
entries.note: BApp store URL changes; resolve the current listing from the store rather than trusting a fixed path.

entries.name: Keycloak (as a test IdP)
entries.role: A real IdP you control, so OAuth redirect, scope and token handling can be tested against something you configured
oracle: redirect accepted to an unregistered URI
entries.note: Most OAuth findings are configuration findings. A local IdP lets you confirm the class before touching a target.

tree.q: Is authentication local, federated, or both?
tree.why: The attack set is almost disjoint. Local auth is about policy and enumeration. Federation is about assertion and redirect handling.

next.q: Is there any lockout or rate limit on the login endpoint?

branches.action: test one account first to confirm, then enumerate and test credentials at a controlled rate
branches.oracle: valid credential or a distinguishable account-exists response

branches.action: treat lockout as the target: is it per account, per IP or global, and can it deny service to a victim
branches.oracle: lockout triggered for a victim without an attempt from you

next.q: Can you see the assertion or token?

branches.action: test signature handling, algorithm, audience and replay before anything else
test redirect URI handling, scope, state and nonce first. those are configuration classes and need no token
branches.oracle: code or token delivered to a URI you control

branches.action: test registration and assertion separately. attestation, origin and user verification are three different checks
branches.oracle: assertion accepted for the wrong origin or user

mirror.detect: failed login distribution per IP and per account
mirror.control: rate limit per account, not per IP

mirror.detect: response or timing difference for unknown accounts
alg or kid mismatch at the verifier
mirror.control: fixed algorithm, no negotiation from the token

mirror.detect: signature not verified over the signed element
mirror.control: validate signature over the canonical element, reject unsigned

mirror.detect: repeated push approves for one account
mirror.control: number matching, rate limit, phishing resistant factors
rotate the session on privilege change

gaps.gap: No tool simulates device code phishing end to end against a tenant you own
gaps.build_candidate: a harness that requests a device code, presents it, and measures whether consent produces a usable token plus the audit trail it leaves

gaps.gap: No passkey attestation analyser that reports what was actually verified
gaps.build_candidate: parse the attestation object, report origin, RP id hash, UV and sign counter behaviour

gaps.gap: No tool measures MFA fatigue resistance as a property rather than a demo
gaps.build_candidate: bounded push loop with number matching analysis and a detection expectation

gaps.gap: L10 impact, L11 retest, L12 drift cells are empty
gaps.build_candidate: account takeover framing template plus a replay based retest and an IdP config drift monitor
